pages.title: Getting started
pages.lede: IGN 26 is a Linux distribution built in Indonesia. These guides take you from downloading it to using it every day.

blocks.p: IGN 26 comes as a live image. You write it to a USB stick, start your computer from it, and use the full desktop without touching your disk. If you want to keep it, the installer puts it on your disk in a few minutes.

head: Part
Minimum
table: 4 GB. 8 GB if you want Android apps.
UEFI. Almost every computer made since 2012 has it.
2 GB or larger. Everything on it will be erased.

pages.title: Download and write to USB
pages.lede: Download the IGN 26 image and put it on a USB stick you can start your computer from.

blocks.note: Writing the image erases everything on the USB stick. Copy off anything you want to keep first.

blocks.p: The current image is **IGN 26 Beta 6**. The file is about 1.3 GB.
Download it in your browser: [ign26-bayu-beta6.iso](https://r2.igos-nusantara.or.id/iso/beta/ign26-bayu-beta6.iso). Or in a terminal:

There is also a nightly image, built every day from the newest code: [ign26-bayu-harian-latest.iso](https://r2.igos-nusantara.or.id/iso/nightly/ign26-bayu-harian-latest.iso). Use it to try changes before the next beta. It may have new bugs.
Plug in the USB stick, then list your disks:
Find the stick by its size and model, for example `sdb`. Make sure it is not the disk your system runs from.
Write the image. Replace `sdX` with the name you found:

cmd: sudo dd if=ign26-bayu-beta6.iso of=/dev/sdX bs=4M status=progress oflag=sync

blocks.p: The stick is ready when the prompt comes back.

blocks.h: Write it on Windows or macOS

blocks.p: Use [balenaEtcher](https://etcher.balena.io). It is free and works the same on both.

steps: Open balenaEtcher and click **Flash from file**. Choose the `.iso` file you downloaded.
Click **Select target** and choose your USB stick.
Click **Flash!** and wait until it says the flash is complete.

blocks.note: On Windows you can also use [Rufus](https://rufus.ie). If it asks how to write the image, choose **DD Image mode**.

blocks.h: Or try it in a virtual machine

blocks.p: You can start the image in GNOME Boxes, virt-manager or VirtualBox instead of a USB stick. Give the machine at least 4 GB of memory and a 25 GB disk, and turn on UEFI. In VirtualBox that is **Settings → System → Enable EFI**.
Next: [start the live session](live.html).

pages.title: Start the live session
pages.lede: Start your computer from the USB stick and try IGN 26 without installing it.

steps: Plug in the USB stick and turn the computer on. Straight away, press the key that opens the boot menu. It is often **F12**, **F11**, **F9** or **Esc**. The first screen usually tells you which one.
Choose the USB stick from the list.

steps.t: The IGN 26 menu appears. Press **Enter** on **Start IGOS Nusantara 26**, or wait three seconds and it starts by itself.
steps.alt: The IGN 26 boot menu with Start IGOS Nusantara 26 selected

steps.t: The desktop starts and opens the installer, Nabau. You can install now, or close Nabau and look around first. Its icon stays in the dock.
steps.alt: The live desktop with the Nabau installer open at step 1

blocks.note: The live session starts in Indonesian. You choose your language in the first step of Nabau, and the installed system uses it.

blocks.h: What works in the live session

blocks.p: Everything: Files, Terminal, Settings, Bayu Store and the network. Nothing is saved to your disk. Files you create and apps you install are gone when you restart.
Restart, and in the menu choose **Start IGOS Nusantara 26 (basic graphics)**. It uses a simpler display driver that works on more graphics cards.
**Troubleshooting** in the boot menu has two more ways to start:

list: **verbose** prints every message while the system starts, so you can see where it stops.
**without the Broadcom wl driver** is for computers with Broadcom Wi-Fi that stop while starting.

blocks.p: Next: [install with Nabau](install.html).

pages.title: Install with Nabau
pages.lede: Nabau puts IGN 26 on your disk in eight steps. Nothing is written until you click Begin installation in step 7.

blocks.note: The automatic layout erases the whole disk you choose. Back up your files before you start.

blocks.p: Nabau opens by itself in the live session. If you closed it, click its icon in the dock.

blocks.note: The screenshots show Nabau in English. For now Nabau stays in Indonesian after step 1, even if you choose English ([issue #42](https://github.com/igos-nusantara/bayu/issues/42)). The buttons are in the same place, and the installed system uses the language you chose.

steps.t: **Language.** Choose the language for the installed system and a regional format. The format decides how dates, numbers and money look. The **Preview** box shows an example. Click **Continue**.
steps.alt: Nabau step 1, Language, with English selected

steps.t: **Network.** A connection is optional, but it lets Nabau set the clock. Wired connections connect by themselves. **Host name** is your computer's name on the network; you can leave it.
steps.alt: Nabau step 2, Network, showing a wired connection

steps.t: **Localization.** Choose the keyboard layout you type with. Type a few letters in **Test the layout** to check it. The time zone is found from your network; change **Region** and **City** if it is wrong.
steps.alt: Nabau step 3, keyboard layout and time zone

steps.t: **Destination.** Select the disk. Keep **Automatic** unless you know which partitions you want. Turn on **Encrypt my data** if the computer could be lost or stolen: you will then type a password every time it starts.
steps.alt: Nabau step 4, choosing the disk and the automatic layout

steps.t: **Software.** **IGN 26 Desktop** is the desktop you are using now. The add-ons on the right are optional, and you can install them later with `dnf`.
steps.alt: Nabau step 5, the IGN 26 Desktop and optional add-ons

steps.t: **Account.** Type your full name; the user name fills in by itself. Type a password twice. Leave **Make this user an administrator** on, so you can install software and change system settings.
steps.alt: Nabau step 6, creating the user account

steps.t: **Review.** Check the summary. Click **Edit** on a card to change it. When it is right, click **Begin installation**. This is the moment the disk is erased.
steps.alt: Nabau step 7, the review screen with the Begin installation button

steps.t: **Install.** Wait until it finishes. On our test machine it took under two minutes; a slow USB stick or disk takes longer.
When you see **You're all set**, take out the USB stick, then click **Restart now**.
steps.alt: Nabau showing You're all set after the installation

steps.t: The sign-in screen shows your name. Type your password and press **Enter**.
steps.alt: The sign-in screen with the user Sari Wulandari

steps.t: A welcome window offers a short tour of the desktop. Click **Start the tour**, or **Skip**.

blocks.p: The image can be a few days old. Open **Terminal** from the dock and run:
Next: [use the desktop](desktop.html).

pages.title: Use the desktop
pages.lede: Find your way around Bayu: the top bar, the dock, the launcher and Settings.

blocks.alt: The Bayu desktop with the top bar and the dock
blocks.caption: The top bar runs across the top. The dock sits at the bottom.

blocks.p: On the left is the IGN logo, then the name of the app in front and that app's menus. Click the logo for **Settings**, **Lock screen**, **Log out**, **Restart** and **Shutdown**.
On the right are the network, **Control Center** and the clock. Control Center has quick switches for Wi-Fi, **Dark Mode**, **Do Not Disturb**, the camera and the microphone.

From left to right: **Launcher**, **Files**, **Terminal**, **Settings**, **Screenshot** and the **Trash**. An app you open gets its own icon until you close it. A dot under an icon means the app is open.
Click the rocket icon to see every installed app. Click one to open it. Press **Esc** to close the launcher.

blocks.alt: The launcher showing all installed apps

blocks.p: Open **Settings** from the dock. Pages are grouped into **Network**, **Desktop**, **Devices** and **System**.

steps: Click **Add language…** and choose a language.
Drag it to the top of the list. The top language is the system language.
Click the logo in the top-left corner, choose **Log out**, and sign in again. Apps then use the new language.

blocks.p: Open **Wallpaper** in Settings. Pictures under **Dynamic** change through the day. Pictures under **System** and **Your wallpapers** stay the same.

blocks.alt: The Wallpaper page in Settings with the two dynamic sets and today's times
blocks.caption: The times shown are for today in your time zone.

steps: Under **Dynamic**, click the mountain or the forest. The mountain is the default.
Next to **Changes with**, choose **Time of day** or **Theme**.

head: Changes with
What you see
table: The **Morning**, **Day**, **Evening** and **Night** pictures, each from the time shown next to it. The times follow sunrise and sunset in your time zone.
The day picture in light mode, the night picture in dark mode.

blocks.p: To use your own picture, click **Add wallpaper**. The login screen uses the same wallpaper as the desktop.
Next: [install apps](apps.html).

pages.title: Install apps
pages.lede: Bayu Store installs Linux apps from Flathub and Android apps from F-Droid, from one search.

blocks.p: Open **Bayu Store** from the launcher. The first time, it downloads the list of apps. This takes a minute or two and happens once.

blocks.alt: Bayu Store showing the Discover page

blocks.p: Type in the search box at the top and press **Enter**. Results from Flathub and F-Droid appear together. Use **Flathub** or **F-Droid** under the title to show only one of them.

blocks.alt: Search results for calculator from Flathub and F-Droid

steps.t: Click the app's name to open its page. It shows who makes it, its licence, the download size and what the app may access.
steps.alt: The page for the GNOME Calculator app

steps: Click **Install**. The button shows the progress.
When the button says **Open**, the app is installed. Click **Open**, or find it in the launcher.

blocks.p: Apps from F-Droid are Android apps. The first one you install asks to turn on Android. See [Android apps](android.html).
Bayu Store installs app updates in the background. To see what changed, open **Updates** in the sidebar. To turn this off, open **Store settings** and switch off **Install updates automatically**.
Bayu Store updates apps only. To update the system itself, run `sudo dnf upgrade` in Terminal.
Open **Installed** in the sidebar, open the app's page and click the trash can button next to **Open**.
Next: [Android apps](android.html).

pages.title: Android apps
pages.lede: Apps from F-Droid run in Lapis, an Android system that runs next to the desktop. Each app opens in its own window.

list: Turning Android on downloads about 1.3 GB, once. Use a fast connection.

steps.t: In Bayu Store, click **Install** on any F-Droid app. Bayu Store asks **Turn on Android apps?** Click **Turn on**.
steps.alt: The Turn on Android apps dialog in Bayu Store
The password prompt for setting up Android apps

steps: Wait for the download to finish. It runs in the background, and Bayu Store does not show its progress yet. At 10 Mbit/s it takes about 20 minutes.
Android then starts for the first time, which takes about a minute. After that, click **Install** on the app again.

steps.t: When the button says **Open**, click it. The Android app opens in its own window, like any other app.
steps.alt: An Android calculator app running in its own window on the Bayu desktop

blocks.p: You can also turn Android on from **Store settings**, under **Android apps**.

blocks.alt: Store settings with the Android apps section
blocks.caption: Store settings, before Android is turned on.

blocks.p: The Android image comes from SourceForge mirrors, which are sometimes slow. If Bayu Store says **Android apps could not be turned on**, open Terminal and run:
It continues where the download stopped and tries other mirrors by itself. When it finishes, install the app again from Bayu Store.

blocks.h: If it says Android is not running

blocks.p: Android needs about a minute to start after you sign in or turn it on. If Bayu Store says **Android container is not running** or **Can't find service: package**, wait a minute and click **Install** again.

Some Android apps are built only for phone processors (ARM). They are hidden by default. To show them, turn on **Show apps built only for ARM** in Store settings. They run through translation, so they are slower and some do not work.

pages.title: Bayu for agents
pages.lede: Bayu can let an AI agent see the screen and use the mouse and keyboard. It only happens after you allow it, and you can stop it with one click.

blocks.p: An agent app, such as Claude Code, talks to `bayu-computer-use`, a small program that speaks MCP (Model Context Protocol). When the agent first asks to see or touch the desktop, Bayu asks you:

blocks.alt: The dialog Let Agent control this computer, with Cancel and Allow buttons

blocks.p: Nothing happens until you click **Allow**. After that:

list: A **Stop** button appears in the top bar while the agent is in control. Click it to stop the agent at once.
When you use the mouse or keyboard yourself, the agent pauses.
The agent cannot answer system dialogs, such as password prompts or this permission dialog.

blocks.alt: The top bar with the stop button next to the network icon
blocks.caption: While an agent is in control, the Stop button sits to the left of the network icon.

blocks.note: `bayu-computer-use` is not in the IGN 26 image yet. Build it from source with the commands below. It takes about a minute.

blocks.p: Install the build tools:
Download only this part of the Bayu source, and build it:
The `rm` line removes a setting meant for Debian builds. Without it, the build cannot download what it needs.

Then **log out and sign in again** (click the logo in the top-left corner, then **Log out**). Bayu looks for `/usr/bin/bayu-computer-use` when you sign in, and trusts only the program at that exact path.
For Claude Code:
For other agent apps, add an MCP server that runs `/usr/bin/bayu-computer-use` over stdio, with no arguments. Many apps use this format:
Start the agent app from the desktop, for example in Terminal. The permission dialog shows the agent's name and the app it runs in.
These are the tools `bayu-computer-use` gives the agent:

head: Tool
What it does
table: Captures the whole screen, or one window
Shows one area of the screen at full resolution, to read small text
Moves the pointer to a point and clicks
Moves the pointer, for example to hover
Presses at one point, moves to another and releases
Presses or releases a mouse button, for drags `drag` cannot do
Types text where the keyboard focus is
Presses a key or shortcut, such as `ctrl+s`
Holds a key down for a while
Brings a window to the front
Closes a window, like its close button
Opens a file, folder or web address
Runs several of these in a row

blocks.p: If the agent reports **This session does not let bayu-computer-use control the computer**, the program is not where Bayu expects it, or you have not logged out and back in since you installed it. Check that `/usr/bin/bayu-computer-use` exists, then log out and sign in again.

pages.title: Troubleshooting
pages.lede: Common problems and what to do about them.

blocks.h: The computer does not start from the USB stick

list: Open the boot menu with the right key (often **F12**, **F11**, **F9** or **Esc**) and pick the stick by hand.
Try another USB port, preferably one directly on the computer.
Write the stick again. On Windows, use **DD Image mode** in Rufus, or use balenaEtcher.

blocks.p: Restart and choose **Start IGOS Nusantara 26 (basic graphics)** in the boot menu.

In the boot menu, open **Troubleshooting** and choose the **verbose** entry. The last lines on screen show where it stops. If your computer has Broadcom Wi-Fi, try the entry **without the Broadcom wl driver**.

blocks.h: Nabau stays in Indonesian after I choose English

blocks.p: This is a known problem ([issue #42](https://github.com/igos-nusantara/bayu/issues/42)). The installed system still uses the language you chose. Every step has its buttons in the same place in every language, so you can follow [Install with Nabau](install.html) as it is.

blocks.h: Android apps could not be turned on

blocks.p: Usually the 1.3 GB download stopped. Run `sudo lapis init -type VANILLA` in Terminal; it continues where it stopped. See [Android apps](android.html#download-stops).

Open an issue at [github.com/igos-nusantara/bayu/issues](https://github.com/igos-nusantara/bayu/issues). Say what you did, what you expected and what happened instead, and attach a screenshot if you can.
